reference_aircraft: Gulfstream G650ER (2 x Rolls-Royce BR725 A1-12), ultra-long-range business jet
description: Twin-turbofan, swept-wing, T-tail business jet. Simulation reference: G650ER, from public specifications only; the public name is fictional. Structural frame: origin at the nose tip, x forward, y right, z down (metres); the fuselage centreline is z = 0.

sources.citation: Aircraft dealer specification sheets for in-service G650ER airframes (e.g. Guardian Jet, S/N 6230; Jetcraft G650ER overview, 2021), which transcribe the AFM weight limits; not the AFM itself.

Manufacturer's published G650ER specifications (dimensions, weights, fuel capacity, range, Mmo, ceiling) and EASA/FAA type certificate data sheet T00015AT (G650 series: Vmo 340 KCAS, Mmo 0.925, flap and gear speeds).
EASA type certificate data sheet E.088 (Rolls-Royce Deutschland BR700-725A1-12): take-off thrust 75.2 kN (16,900 lbf); bypass ratio 4.4 (manufacturer).
J. D. Mattingly, Elements of Gas Turbine Propulsion (McGraw-Hill, 1996), eq. 2.54a: installed thrust lapse of a high-bypass turbofan.
J. Roskam, Airplane Design Part V/VI: radii of gyration and drag build-up for business jets.
Engineering estimate for this simulation (no published source); see the note.

provenance.note: BR725 fan diameter 50 in (1.27 m, manufacturer). Windmilling drag area 0.12 x the fan disc (1.267 m^2) = 0.152 m^2 of CdA, after Torenbeek App. G (windmilling high-bypass turbofan ~0.1 q x inlet area); about 0.55 kN at 150 KTAS at sea level.
Two engine-driven starter-generators in parallel (the G650ER's two 40 kVA generators, here 300 A each on a 28 V DC bus), each on line from 45 % N2; bus minimum 18 V (24 V system).

Essential bus with automatic load shedding: with no generator on line the bus controller sheds the non-essential loads 2 s after the battery alone takes the bus (the G650's essential/emergency buses keep PFD 1, standby instruments, COM 1/NAV 1, engine indication, boost pumps and probe heat after a dual generator loss); the split of the avionics load (10 A essential, 15 A shed) and the load currents are estimates for a 28 V system. Roughly doubles the 40 Ah battery's endurance.

Two 3,000 psi systems, each with an engine-driven pump (A: left, B: right), A also with an electric pump that needs generator power; gear, flaps, spoilers, nose-wheel steering and brakes on either system; brake accumulator good for 6 applications; free-fall gear extension at 35 % of the normal rate. Layout after the G650's two-system arrangement, numbers estimated.
Yaw damper (the G650ER has one): washed-out yaw rate (3 s) to the rudder, 2 per rad/s at 160 KEAS scheduled with 1/EAS^2, 30 % authority.
Wing area 119.2 m^2 (1283 ft^2), span 30.36 m (99 ft 7 in), length 30.41 m; MAC from the modelled planform.
MTOW 103,600 lb; MLW 83,500 lb; max fuel 48,200 lb.
Maximum ramp weight 104,000 lb (dealer specification sheets; consistent across serial numbers).
Maximum zero fuel weight 60,500 lb (dealer specification sheets).
The empty mass is derived from a basic operating weight, which includes unusable fuel and oil.
Basic operating weight ~54,000 lb less a crew of two and catering.
Business-jet radii of gyration Rx 0.30, Ry 0.33, Rz 0.45.

Planform matching the published area and span (30.36 m including the winglets); quarter-chord sweep 27/33 deg; supercritical section polar, clmax 1.8 at flight Reynolds numbers (~2e7). Span loading by the nonlinear lifting line: with 6 deg of washout (incidence 0 / -0.7 / -6 deg root / kink / tip) the clean wing reaches CLmax ~1.22 (1.28 before the sweep stall progression below), near the published ~112 KIAS clean stall at mid weight. Winglets estimated from photographs: canted 75 deg, ~1.6 m tall, 40 deg sweep, chords 1.8 / 0.6 m, toed out 3 deg. Single-slotted Fowler flaps to ~70 % semi-span (meeting the ailerons), 25 % chord, extending the chord 12 % at full deflection, dclmax/dcl 0.9 (landing CLmax ~2.08; 1-g stall ~100 KIAS at mid weight). Tailplane incidence -0.8 deg (stabiliser neutral) for a ~1.7 deg cruise attitude.
The G650 trims with a movable horizontal stabiliser; travel (10 deg nose up, 3 deg nose down) estimated for the class, not published.

Take-off thrust and bypass ratio published; lapse coefficient 0.18 (Mattingly's 0.49 for airliner engines) calibrated so Mach 0.85 is available up to FL510 at mid weight (max-cruise thrust near the ceiling); TSFC 0.39 static / ~0.60 cruise (Estimated).
Equivalent flat-plate areas from a wetted-area build-up (CD0 ~ 0.018); fuselage and nacelle transonic drag rise from Mcrit 0.86 / 0.84 (Estimated).
Vmo 340 KCAS, Mmo 0.925; flap speeds 250/220/170 KCAS (10/20/39 deg) and VLE 250 KCAS are representative (Estimated).
Rudder travel limiter: full 25 deg travel to 160 KEAS, then scaled with 1/q (about 10 deg at 250 KEAS), typical of business jets with a rudder limiter.
Oleo stiffness and damping sized for static deflection ~0.14 m and ~0.4 critical damping at MTOW.
Typical of large business jets (G650 figures not public): mains ~190 psi (hydroplaning ~124 kt), nose ~160 psi.

Static loads at MTOW from the geometry (nose 36.8 kN, each main bogie 211.5 kN); the cornering stiffness is the value at that load and follows the usual load sensitivity above and below it. Spin inertia of a twin-wheel main bogie with its brake rotors ~50 kg m^2, the twin nose wheels ~5.5 kg m^2.

Carbon brakes as a torque capacity of 59 kN m per main bogie at full pedal (the former force-coefficient model, 0.5 x load, at the static load): ~0.45 g at MTOW with the wing unloaded, the usual certification maximum, and more than the tyres hold while the wing still carries weight, where the anti-skid limits them. Digital anti-skid at 88 % efficiency (the fraction of the peak braking force held; modern systems 0.85-0.92).
Hydraulic nose-wheel steering: tiller +-80 deg (typical of large business jets; G650 figure not public), rudder pedals +-10 deg. Actuator slew 20 deg/s, estimated.

Three spoiler panels per side ahead of the outboard flap (photographs), 14 % chord, 40 deg at full speedbrake; their drag (~1.6 m^2 CdA fully out) and lift loss (~25 % of the wing's) match the lumped speedbrake estimate they replace.

FADEC thrust ratings as fractions of the sea-level static take-off thrust: maximum continuous 0.92, maximum climb 0.88, maximum cruise 0.84 (typical of modern business-jet turbofans: MCT 0.90-0.93, MCL 0.85-0.90, MCR 0.80-0.87), take-off limited to 5 min (10 min with an engine out). Modelled as turbine-temperature limits: each rating holds a fixed fraction of the temperature-limited thrust (Mattingly's temperature branch continued below the throttle ratio), so the fractions apply at sea level and the ratings converge on the flat-rated line at altitude, where the take-off rating itself is far below its temperature limit (at FL410 the maximum-cruise rating allows 97 % of the lapse-law thrust). The lapse coefficient's earlier calibration (Mach 0.85 to FL510 at mid weight) therefore stands.

Fan-flow (cascade) reversers: reverse force 40% of the forward thrust at the same N1 (typical of high-bypass fan reversers), 2 s transit, 80% N1 in reverse, reverse idle and stow at 60 KIAS (a usual airline technique). Automatic: deploy on main-wheel contact at idle.
Ground spoilers: every panel to full on main-wheel contact with the throttles at idle above 30 kt ground speed (a landing or a rejected take-off); stowed when the throttles come up or below 15 kt.

Buffet boundary: the section's clmax falls as 1 - 5 (Mn - 0.5)^2 above a normal Mach number of 0.5 (Mn = M cos(sweep); simple sweep theory as the Korn drag rise), floor 0.35. Shape after the CL-buffet-onset curves of supercritical transport wings (Obert, Aerodynamic Design of Transport Aircraft, ch. 20): the trimmed 1-g CLmax falls from 1.27 at low speed to 0.90 at M0.85 (71 %), a 1.3-g buffet margin at CL ~0.7, in the range of the class at FL410 mid weight. No G650 buffet-onset data published.

Swept-wing stall progression: the boundary layer drifts outboard along the swept span, so the outboard sections stall below the section's clmax and the inboard above it, and past the stall the inboard sections keep carrying high loads while the separated outboard flow drains toward the tips (Harper & Maki, NACA TN 2947; Furlong & McHugh, NACA Rep. 1339). The section's lift limits and its separated normal force (Viterna's CDmax) are scaled by 1 - 0.5 sin(sweep) (eta - 1/2): tips -14 %, roots +11 % at the 27/33 deg sweeps, the order of the section-clmax spread reported for 30-45 deg sweeps. Effect: the stall begins outboard of mid-semispan (the 6 deg of washout no longer holds the tips through it), the wing-body moment at 20 deg is nose-up by ~0.09 against the uniform polar's (the pitch-up past the stall, DATCOM 4.1.3.4; AR 7.7 at 33 deg is on the pitch-up side of the Shortal-Maggin boundary), the clean trimmed CLmax falls from 1.28 to 1.22 (the clean 1-g stall ~114 KIAS at mid weight), the landing CLmax and Vref are unchanged (2.00, 121 KIAS at MLW), the AoA computer's warning (least strip margin, now the tip's) moves from 120 to 124 KIAS. Below the stall nothing changes. It does not lock the T-tail deep stall in (tests/test_jet.cpp, docs/fidelity-matrix.md). No G650 stall-progression or post-stall data published.

Mach tuck: through the drag rise (Mcrit = Korn Mdd - 0.1077 to Mdd + 0.05) the rear-loaded supercritical section's aft loading grows (cm0 shift -0.06, the order of the cm(M) trend of NASA SC(2) sections, Harris NASA TP-2969), and from about Mdd the section's force point moves aft from c/4 toward c/2 at M1 (thin-airfoil limits; Hilton, High-Speed Aerodynamics, 1951; Raymer 12.4.2). Stabiliser trimmed at FL410 M0.80 and the speed raised, the 1-g pitching moment reverses from nose up to nose down in the mid-0.8s and is a push at M0.92; the elevator per g about triples toward Mmo (figures in tests/test_transonic.cpp). No G650 trim-vs-Mach data published.

Hinged-control effectiveness x max(0.2, 1 - (M/Mdd0)^10), Mdd0 the zero-lift Korn Mdd of the surface (0.95 for the tailplane): the shock standing ahead of the hinge line unloads the flap. Elevator pitching power at M0.92 is 29 % of its M0.5 value, 91 % at M0.80 (Hilton 1951 on control effectiveness through the transonic range). No G650 data.

T-tail deep stall: the stalled wing's separated wake leaves the mid-chord at (alpha - downwash) with half-thickness c/2 sin(alpha - eps) plus 0.16 per metre aft (a turbulent wake's ~9 deg half-angle), as strong as the wing's separated fraction; inside it the tail (6 m above the wing plane, ~12 m behind the mid-chord) sees 20 % of the dynamic pressure at the core (the ~55 % velocity deficit a few chords behind a stalled wing; Taylor & Ray, AIAA 65-737: the tail's pitching contribution nearly lost in the wake) and the downwash of the wing at its CLmax rather than one falling with the collapsing lift. The tail is in the wake from alpha ~25 to ~40 deg. Without the stick pusher, full aft stick at idle settles into a deep stall near 40 deg of alpha (1 g, ~7,000 fpm) with the elevator's pitching power below 15 % of its unstalled value; the pusher keeps the airplane out of it. The airframe still pitches down on its own once the stick goes forward (no swept-wing post-stall pitch-up in the regularised lifting line), so the model does not lock in.
